themes_detail.label: Building Safety Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Flooring and stair safety complaints spiked to 5 THIS WEEK compared to a 2.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 110% increase (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting potential widespread structural or maintenance issues in residential or commercial buildings across Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 5 flooring/stairs complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)
High z-score (5.42) indicates statistically significant anomaly
reporting_angles: Investigate which buildings are filing complaints and whether landlords are responding to repair requests
Interview residents about fall hazards and whether DOB inspections have been conducted

themes_detail.label: Enforcement Activity Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Real Time Enforcement complaints jumped 1500% to 8 complaints last week from a baseline of 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 10.61)—the highest statistical spike in the dataset—indicating a major enforcement operation or policy change is unfolding in the district this week.
evidence: 8 Real Time Enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 10.61, highest spike)
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD and City enforcement agencies to determine what enforcement operation triggered the spike
Clarify whether this is parking, quality-of-life, or another enforcement category and its duration

themes_detail.label: Park Rule Violations and Animal Issues
themes_detail.summary: Park-related complaints surged in the last week: Violation of Park Rules up 2300% (3 complaints vs. 0.1 baseline, z-score: 8.69) and Animal in a Park up 380% (9 complaints vs. 1.9 baseline, z-score: 5.62), suggesting potential overcrowding, unsupervised animals, or park maintenance failures affecting Fort Greene Park or Brooklyn Bridge Park.
evidence: Violation of Park Rules: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.1 average (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Animal in a Park: 9 complaints last week vs. 1.9 average (380% increase, z-score: 5.62)
Both spikes occurred in the same reporting period, suggesting related park conditions
reporting_angles: Visit Fort Greene Park and Brooklyn Bridge Park to document specific rule violations and animal issues
Interview Parks Department about patrol frequency and recent changes to park rules or policies

themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Jump
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints spiked 500% to 6 complaints last week versus a 1.0 weekly average (z-score: 7.07), indicating potential illegal conversions, unpermitted occupancy changes, or unauthorized commercial use in residential buildings across the district.
evidence: 6 Building/Use complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (500% increase, z-score: 7.07)
1193 total DOB permits filed in last 90 days (861 alterations) suggests heavy construction activity that may include illegal work
Three active ULURP rezonings (including 395 Flatbush Avenue redevelopment) indicate development pressure in the district
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with DOB violation records to identify patterns of illegal conversions
Interview DOB about enforcement capacity given development pressure from ongoing ULURP applications

themes_detail.label: Street Sign and Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Street Sign - Damaged complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 10 complaints versus a 1.9 weekly average (433% increase, z-score: 5.96), though this spike has partially receded, it signals broader street infrastructure deterioration that has not been fully resolved.
evidence: 10 Street Sign - Damaged complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.9 weekly average (433% increase, z-score: 5.96)
Repeated CB budget requests for 'Other transportation infrastructure requests' suggest ongoing street maintenance gaps
503 Street Condition complaints in 90-day baseline indicate systemic infrastructure maintenance backlog
reporting_angles: Investigate whether sign damage is clustered in specific neighborhoods and if DOT is tracking repairs
Interview community board about why street infrastructure requests recur in annual budget proposals
